questions.question:
4.
  a) Find sin ( A+B ) if sin A = −4/5 and cos B = 15/17
     A and B are in Quadrant IV. Also state Quadrant of ( A + B) ( 4 marks)
  b) Prove that csc ( π + x) = − csc x ( 2 marks)
questions.answer_guide:
a) Quadrant IV: cos A = 3/5, sin B = −8/17
   sin(A + B) = sinA cosB + cosA sinB = (−4/5)(15/17) + (3/5)(−8/17) = −60/85 − 24/85 = −84/85
   cos(A + B) = cosA cosB − sinA sinB = 45/85 − 32/85 = 13/85 > 0 → (A + B) is in Quadrant IV
b) csc(π + x) = 1/sin(π + x) = 1/(sin π cos x + cos π sin x) = 1/(−sin x) = −csc x ∎

questions.section: PART 2: ANSWER ALL QUESTIONS. (60 MARKS)
questions.question:
5.
  a) Verify that sin C + sin D = 2 sin((C + D)/2) cos((C − D)/2) ( 4 MARKS)
  b.) verify that sin∝ cos B = ½ [ sin(∝ + B) + sin(∝ − B) ] ( 2 marks)
questions.answer_guide:
a) Let A = (C + D)/2, B = (C − D)/2, so C = A + B and D = A − B.
   sin(A + B) + sin(A − B) = (sinA cosB + cosA sinB) + (sinA cosB − cosA sinB) = 2 sinA cosB
   → sin C + sin D = 2 sin((C + D)/2) cos((C − D)/2) ∎
b) RHS = ½[(sin∝ cosB + cos∝ sinB) + (sin∝ cosB − cos∝ sinB)] = ½(2 sin∝ cosB) = sin∝ cosB = LHS ∎

6.
  a) Convert y² = 4x into a polar coordinate ( 3 marks)
  b.) Convert r² + 4 r cos θ - 8 r sin θ = -4 to Cartesian equation ( 3 marks)
questions.answer_guide:
a) x = r cos θ, y = r sin θ: r² sin²θ = 4r cos θ → r = 4 cos θ / sin²θ = 4 cot θ csc θ
b) x² + y² + 4x − 8y = −4 → (x + 2)² + (y − 4)² = 16 (circle, centre (−2, 4), radius 4)
